page: Amazon Web Services r9g.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by 64-bit ARMv9 AWS Graviton processors based on the Neoverse-V3 core design. The instance provides 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, running at a clock rate of 3.3 GHz. Each core includes 64 KB of L1 data cache and 2 MB of L2 cache, backed by 48 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity is 32.0 GB, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include integrated GPUs or local NVMe storage, relying on external network storage, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-thread efficiency and memory subsystem throughput. In synthetic memory testing, the instance achieved a top-tier PassMark memory score of 4013.91, alongside read-only cached bandwidth of 525.78 GB/sec and uncached memory reads of 111.11 GB/sec. Single-threaded performance tests demonstrate top-tier results in Geekbench single-core execution (2374.0), text processing (3052.0), single-threaded gzip compression (36.34 GB/sec), and bzip3 decompression (17.13 GB/sec). General multi-core tests, including Geekbench multi-core (7792.0) and stress-ng multi-core (7967.31), perform within the average middle tier.

Tradeoffs are evident in compute-heavy and machine learning workloads. Because it operates with 4 cores without hardware accelerators, PassMark CPU testing ranks in the lower tiers, and larger language model inference demonstrates weak throughput, logging 8.51 tokens per second on a 7B parameter model. However, for in-memory processing, it sustains 12.09 million Redis SET operations per second and 18.32 GB/sec in static web serving. The instance presents solid qualitative cost efficiency for memory-dense, cache-dependent enterprise applications, making it suitable for in-memory caching layers, relational database hosting, and memory-intensive web workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services r9g.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by a 4-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-V3 ARMv9 processor clocked at 3.3 GHz. Configured on the Nitro hypervisor with dedicated physical cores, it supplies 32.0 GB of memory (8.0 GB per vCPU) and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. The instance omits local ephemeral storage and GPU acceleration. Benchmarks show top-tier memory scores and strong single-thread performance, including high text processing, gzip compression, and decompression rates. While limited core counts lead to lower performance in large language model inference and heavy numerical compute tests, it maintains average Redis throughput of 12.09 million SET operations per second. The r9g.xlarge is well balanced for memory-intensive services, in-memory key-value caching, data processing, and relational databases.
